results.title: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?
results.content: The Taliban rulers in Afghanistan have accused Pakistan of aiding and sheltering armed resistance groups. The allegations come amid heightened tensions and are likely to deepen the rift between the two neighbors.

results.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
results.content: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

results.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
results.content: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

results.title: Africa at COP31: Will climate cash finally flow?
results.content: As the curtains draw to a close on COP31 in Antalya, one question looms large for African countries: Will climate promises finally translate into the funding African communities need to cope with a warming world?

results.title: Myanmar genocide ruling: Rohingya say struggle for justice not over
results.content: The ICJ has held Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya and ordered restitution and reparations. Community members have hailed the ruling, but caution that achieving real change will be long and hard.

results.title: China's Xi praises 'turnaround' in relationship with Australia
results.content: The leaders of Australia and China have held talks on sidelines of APEC summit. Australian PM Anthony Albanese is also slated to meet Chinese Premier Li Qiang.

results.title: White House replaces cyber security chief after tech outages
results.content: Sean Cairncross is leaving his role as national cyber director after a chaotic week of tech outages. Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, will assume the position in an acting capacity.

results.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
results.content: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

results.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
results.content: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

results.title: Iraq's risky standoff: The state vs. Iran-allied militias
results.content: This week, Iraqi security forces surrounded an area run by the Kataib Hezbollah militia. Onlookers describe it as the most dangerous confrontation between the Iraqi state and Iran-allied militias in decades.

results.title: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have held trilateral talks ― but what did they achieve?
results.content: The presidents of China, the US and Russia have held an unprecedented summit. While Trump said the three leaders were "making history," Xi described the talks as "fruitful" and Putin called them "open and candid."
